I'm working out the rule: from each corner marker, draw concentric square outlines at increasing Chebyshev distance, then clip each region to the cells closest to that marker using a Voronoi-style comparison against the other markers on the 17x17 grid with markers at (0,0), (16,0), and (16,16).

Comparing Manhattan distances, I derive that marker 4 owns cells where i<8 and i+j<16, marker 8 owns cells where i>8 and j<8, and marker 1 owns cells where i+j>16 and j>8, and now I'm resolving the tie-breaking along the boundary lines i=8, j=8, and i+j=16.

I'm now building the 17x17 grid row by row, checking each cell against these region conditions plus the Chebyshev parity requirement to decide whether it gets colored.

Finishing row1's pattern, then computing row2 with max(2,j) logic giving mostly alternating 4s and 0s, and starting row3's max(3,j) evaluation similarly.

Continuing the pattern, row6 has 4s at even j up to 6 then j=8, row7 only has a 4 at j=8, and now I'm working out row8's region where max(a,b) stays even while a+b remains under 16.

For row8, j from 9 to 16 all give max=8 which is even, so those all become 1, giving nine zeros followed by eight ones. Now checking row9, I find no valid j for the 8-region since max(7,j) is odd for j≤7, so I'm moving into the 1-region checking parity of max(7, 16-j) for j>7.

Row10 with a=6 gives j=0 through 6 valid for the 8-region since max(6,j)=6 stays even, but j=7 fails since max becomes 7. For the 1-region, I'm checking b=16-j against a=6, finding j=10 through 16 satisfy the even condition while j=9 fails with max=7.

Continuing to row11 with a=5: only j=6 works in the 8-region (since max(5,6)=6 is even), and only j=10 works in the 1-region (max(5,6)=6 even). Then moving to row12 with a=4, I'm checking which j values keep max(4,j) even in both regions, finding j=0-4 and j=6 work on one side, and starting to evaluate the symmetric case on the other side.

Finishing row14 with j10,12,14,15,16 set to 1. Row15 gives j2,4,6=8 and j10,12,14=1. Row16 with a=0 sets 8-values at even j through 6, and 1-values at even j from 10 to 16.

Now I'm double-checking the boundary cases: row10's j=7 correctly falls outside the 8-region since max(6,7)=7 is odd, and the row0 j=0 marker is consistently 4 as expected. Comparing against the earlier 7x7 example where row3 was all zeros, this pattern holds together properly.

I'm working row by row to figure out which cells in the 9-region satisfy the even-max condition for coloring, then mirroring the same logic for the 2-region on the other side.

Filling out the remaining rows with the same mirrored pattern, then I pause to double-check against the example grid, since my row2 output doesn't match the expected values there—I need to re-examine how the ring values for 1 should actually be computed.
